To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) statistical association measures and word frequency can be used as indicators for MWE identification; (2) there is no single threshold that can be used for all MWE, but the thresholds must be adapted for each type of MWE; (3) the MI values of MWE are highly variable, depending on the type and the frequency of the MWE; (4) the MI values are not always the best indicators of MWE, and other measures can be used for specific cases

(1) statistical measures and frequency are important for the identification of collocations; (2) statistical measures are not important for the identification idioms; (3) frequency is important for the identification light verbs + predicate and (4) frequency and MI are important for the identifi- cation of nominal compounds.

(1) the statistical measure is a necessary but not sufficient condition to identify MWE; (2) the MI values are very low for a large proportion of the MWE in our gold dataset; (3) the frequency is not a reliable measure to identify MWE and (4) the MI measure is not a reliable criterion to establish the cutting point between MWE and n-grams.
